description: The single documented additional-harness candidate assessed under task 5.1 / GATE-E04: codex-cli reached through `hermes codex-runtime` — the only migration path the Hermes boundary map documents (external CLI worker lanes are otherwise a recorded no-go). This file is the assessment's input record: identity, provenance, measured demand signals, incremental maintenance surface and the capability/authority matrix claims. It asserts no admission — the probe derives each claim's evidence state from the committed sources and any over-claim is an instrumentation breach.

model.auth: Hermes pooled OAuth (hermes auth list includes openai-codex)

signals.measured: 1 of 6 recruited pilot workloads requested a non-selected runtime (workload_class runtime-mirror); denied as unsupported-workload:runtime-mirror; zero observation events collected
1 of the proposed 2 external maintainers held a 4-week completed streak on the *selected* recipe — repeat-use target failed, so no measured demand base exists for a second lane
0 of 10 cohort issues were blocked or failed for want of a second harness; failures were verification-blocked / attempts-exhausted / canceled / declined

demand.note: no repeated external request and no internal blockage attributable to the selected harness is on record

new_surfaces: candidate version tracking + compatibility matrix per release
adapter-specific §8.2 fault-suite repetitions on top of the existing 19 rows × 57 reps
credential separation and isolation review per admitted lane
support-matrix row + recipe coverage for the second runtime
incremental_maintenance.effort_class: task-5.2 bound: ≤ 3 developer-days — hooks unproven, so the estimate cannot be grounded today
incremental_maintenance.measured_context: cohort setup+maintenance already amortizes to 7.5 min/issue, lifting total burden to 23.5 vs the 23.0 baseline — maintenance erases the per-issue saving before any second lane exists

capability_matrix.claim: executable present + version pinned + model provider pooled; worker-lane readiness/authorization never probed
kanban create/claim/dispatch proven for the Kanban profile worker; a codex-runtime worker lane has never been dispatched
heartbeat/runs/tail/watch supported for the profile worker; candidate lane liveness undemonstrated
kanban complete/block/request-review + attach + pr_acceptance events proven for the profile worker only
separate implement/review profiles exist on the selected lane; the candidate has never run an independent role session
kanban block+reclaim fences the profile worker generation; descendant exit accounting for an external CLI lane is undemonstrated
unblock/reclaim/reassign exist on the selected lane; candidate resume is not presumed — checkpoint/restart is the fallback contract
live steering is a Should-tier capability, deferred by the boundary map; never presumed for any candidate

probes.claim: pooled openai-codex OAuth authorizes the model lane; no current-generation worker authorization exists for a codex-runtime lane
profile-scoped GH_CONFIG_DIR/GH_TOKEN is the documented credential boundary for kanban lanes; candidate worker credentials were never separated or fenced
evidence: hermes-boundary-map.md 'Boundaries that must not be rebuilt' — credential broker row

probes.claim: external CLI worker lanes are not a paved path; only the hermes codex-runtime app-server migration is documented, and it has never been exercised against the kanban contract — a second scheduler remains forbidden
evidence: hermes-boundary-map.md 'Named gaps / no-go list' — external CLI worker lanes + second scheduler rows

probes.claim: the existing preview/human-approved merge endpoint was exercised only through the selected lane, which still carries open live blockers (base-unprotected, telegram-adapter-live, vercel-linkage, kanban-live-write); the candidate has never driven it
